It is identified with {{ill|Takemikakano- Shrine|lt=Takemikakano- Shrine|qid=Q135039639}}, which is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}<ref name="yao">[https://yaokami.jp/1131349/ Daisanōji Shrine] - Eight Million Kami</ref>.<ref>https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=181576</ref>

== Overview ==
The date of foundation is unknown, but as it is identified as a Shikinaisha, its origins are thought to date back to before ancient times.

In {{ill|2019|Q25274|qid=Q25274}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}} 1), the shrine buildings were destroyed by the {{ill|Typhoon Hagibis|Q69841946|qid=Q69841946|lt=typhoon damage}}, and as of 2024 the site remains vacant land with the structures removed<ref>[https://niijima-info.jp/enjoy/attractions/daisansama/ Daisanōji Shrine] - Niijima Village Tourist Information Office</ref>.

== Enshrined deities ==
* Daisanōji Myōjin (大三王子明神) — the prince of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}, Takemikaka-no-Mikoto (多祁美加々命)<ref name="yao"/>.
* Deisanōji Myōjin (弟三王子明神) — his younger brother.
